meta.title: Morgan Hand Mill (MHM) knowledge base
meta.source: The Morgan Hand Mill Manual (chapters A-R, rev. 2005-2013)
meta.author: Tom Morgan Rodsmiths (Tom Morgan & Gerri Carlson), Manhattan, MT
meta.license: Copyrighted manual. This is a DERIVED, factual knowledge base (specs, procedures, and the taper-setting model) summarized in our own words for reference/education. The raw manual PDFs are NOT redistributed (see data/raw/mhm/, gitignored). See docs/MHM.md for the human-readable digest.
meta.why: Grounds caneDNA's Mill Settings and the planned anvil-position visualizer in the actual machine, and validates our MHM computations against the manual's own model.

machine.maker: Tom Morgan Rodsmiths (Tom Morgan & Gerri Carlson), Manhattan, MT

base.desc: Chrome-plated cold-rolled steel bar the plane rides on; the taper reference surface.
base.mounting: Bolts to a 2 x 2 x 3/8 in, 75 in aluminum angle at 7 points so accuracy doesn't depend on bench flatness.
base.capacity: Planes two-piece rods up to ~9 ft and various three-piece rods

adjustable_bed.desc: Steel bar on top of the base, raised above it by push/pull screws every 5 in to set the taper. The anvil sits on the bed; the strip sits on the anvil.
adjustable_bed.stations: #0 through #13 (14 stations) on 5-inch centers, spanning 0-60 in
adjustable_bed.station_zero: #0 has no adjusting screw, only a locking screw; always held tight against the base
adjustable_bed.screws: Push = 5/16-18 flat-head set screws; pull/lock = 1/4-20 cap-head screws

anvils.material: White HDPE with embedded brass inserts (26x 8-32 to mount to bed; 4-40 for butt / 2-56 for tip strip hold-down)
anvils.shipped: 5 anvils: butt-roughing, tip-roughing, butt-finishing, and two tip-finishing
anvils.role: Anvils ONLY support the strip; they do NOT set the taper (the bed does), so anvils don't wear as the taper changes.
anvils.finishing_holddown_stations: 11 lettered hold-down screw positions (A-K) on each finishing anvil
anvils.roughing_holddown_stations: 3 positions (long / medium / short, the short being for ~3-piece rods)
anvils.truing: Finishing anvils must be trued (shaved flat between stations with a carbide insert in the dial-holder/shaver) before use; the factory-installed reference anvil must never be recut. Target trued flatness +/- 0.001 in (0.002 in TIR).

hold_down_letters.meaning: The base has tapped holes on its right front labeled A-K; matching letters are stamped on the bed just below the finishing anvils' 11 hold-down screws.
hold_down_letters.mill_stop: A movable 'mill stop' screws into one lettered hole. It (1) stops the plane so the cutters can't hit the strip's hold-down screw and (2) gives an automatic plane stop matched to the rod section's length.
hold_down_letters.selection_rule: The letters are START / mill-stop positions in the tip region, at 2.5-in pitch, A at the tip end. You start a finish pass just past the tiptop -- the manual's 'start cutting ~6 in from the tip' -- which is ~hole D (7.5 in from the tip, just butt-ward of the tiptop that registers at station #12). So finish milling normally starts at ~D regardless of length; ROUGH-cutting and one-piece / extension-bed setups start at hole A. The strip's tip always sits between stations #12-#13. What varies with section length is which taper stations the section spans (registered from #12 back toward the butt), not the start letter. Worked example (7 ft, 2-piece): finish tip -> hole D, tiptop at station #12 with ~3 in of strip past it.
hold_down_letters.modeling_note: For the caneDNA anvil visualizer: register the section's tiptop/ferrule at station #12 (strip ~3 in past, toward #13); the taper occupies stations back toward the butt, one per 5 in -> this is what varies with section length. The START letter is a separate tip-region position (see below), ~fixed near D for finish milling.
hold_down_letters.observed_labeling: Confirmed from a mill photo (right-hand model, anvil 'RB' = right butt) plus the owner: the bed carries TWO stamped systems. (1) Numbers = the taper STATIONS, running 1-13 (5-in centers). (2) Letters A-K = the START / mill-stop positions. The letters are at 2.5-in pitch (half a station), so the odd letters coincide with stations: A=station1, C=2, E=3, G=4, I=5, K=6 (K is stamped 'K 6'). The A-K letters cover only the tip-most ~25 in (stations 1-6). Finish milling starts ~hole D (~7.5 in from the tip, just past the tiptop at #12 -- the manual's 'start cutting ~6 in from the tip'); rough-cutting and one-piece / extension-bed setups start at hole A. So the start letter is roughly fixed by build type, NOT a function of section length; section length drives the station span instead.

cutter_heads.note: Morgan uses 61.5 deg for 6-strip (not the traditional 60 deg), per Winston practice, to reduce visible glue seams. caneDNA's strip-depth math currently assumes the ideal 60-deg inradius (dimension/2) for hex; the 1.5-deg difference is a possible future refinement.
cutter_heads.inserts: Two carbide inserts, 3 edges each; a set planes ~3-5 rods. Cut depth <= 0.010 in/pass green, 0.001-0.003 in/pass heat-treated.

measuring_block.desc: Caliper-mounted block reading strip height in per-geometry grooves; 6061T6 aluminum.

setting_model.principle: TWO separate steps. (1) SET THE TAPER: with the plane's dial indicator, raise the bed at each 5-in station to the correct height above the base. (2) MILL: measure the STRIP HEIGHT with calipers / the measuring block as you cut and stop at target; a hard stop then repeats it for every strip.
setting_model.station_setting_is: The cumulative rise of the bed at each station relative to a chosen reference station (typically #2 = 0.000). It equals (half-dimension at reference) minus (half-dimension at that station) = caneDNA's MillSetting.total_increase. It is NOT the strip height.
setting_model.strip_height_is: Half the flat-to-flat rod dimension at that station (one strip). Measured during milling, never set by the bed.
setting_model.reference_station: The taper is registered so the strip tip is near the anvil tip; for shorter rods the taper starts at station #2 (or higher), not #0/#1, to avoid cutting the anvil too narrow at its tip.
setting_model.extend_past_length: The taper is continued one or more stations past the rod's end so strips have extra length (Morgan likes >=5-6 in extra, min 3 in on tips) for straight gluing.
setting_model.roddna_caveat: Morgan's own manual (chapter J) says of RodDNA's MHM Settings Report: use the Station #, Increment, Rod Dim, and Increase columns; DISREGARD 'Form Depth' (should be strip height) and 'Settings' (wrong on some tapers). This validates caneDNA computing strip_depth + total_increase itself rather than porting RodDNA's report.
setting_model.hexrod_reference: hexrod.net (Frank Stetzer, with Chris Obuchowski) also has an MHM Settings page: Inches, Rod Dim, Half Dim, MHM Setting, Station.

chapters.title: Title Page & Table of Contents
key_facts: Tom Morgan Rodsmiths, Manhattan MT; www.troutrods.com.
9 top-level sections; accessories: measuring block, hollow fluter, swelled-butt kit, magic star cutter, extension bed, enamel scraper, splitter.

chapters.title: Getting Started
key_facts: Ships with a factory-trued butt-finishing anvil + demo straight taper (0.006 in/station) for practice.
Learn the push/pull screws, dial indicator, and steel weight first; true your own anvils before cutting.
Strip height is found by measuring while cutting, not from the bed setting.

chapters.title: Introduction
chapters.purpose: Design philosophy, components, cutting principle, workflow.
key_facts: Two self-aligning parts: an adjustable plane holding the cutters + an adjustable bed holding the strip; follows the grain.
Cuts both strip sides at once at a fixed bevel; taper set by the bed raising the strip into the cutters.
Redesigned plane (2004, w/ Dennis Detloff) shipping since late 2005; adjustable hard stop (Joe Byrd) repeats finish depth.
Workflow: split -> prep/straighten nodes -> drill anvil hole -> rough cut (taper preset) -> swap anvil -> finish anvil, set taper, finish cut in many light passes.
key_numbers: Dial indicator 0-1 in travel, 0.001 in accuracy
Included angles 46/61.5/73.5/92 deg for 8/6/5/4-strip

chapters.title: Hand Mill Tools
key_facts: Provided: strip/base hold-down screws, weight, 1-in dial indicator, dial holder/shaver, hex wrenches, 5 carbide-insert sets, anvils, 6-strip head, hold-down shoe, aluminum angle, mill stop, swelled-butt kit, plane, sample-taper spreadsheets.
Not provided: bench bolts, micrometer, caliper.
Options: measuring block, hollow fluter, magic star cutter, extension bed, other cutter heads.

chapters.title: Aluminum Angle & Base Mounting
chapters.purpose: Mount the angle to the bench and attach the base.
key_facts: Base bolts to a 2x2x3/8 in, 75 in aluminum angle (idea from John Miller) at 7 points; accuracy no longer depends on bench surface.
Install the angle with a slight ~1/8 in upward bow so the plane doesn't dip in the middle; check level by rocking the plane along the base.
Vertical face has 7 slots on 12-in centers for the anchor screws.

chapters.title: Morgan Hand Mill Plane
chapters.purpose: The plane that cuts the strips; parts, use, insert install.
key_facts: Calibrated dial reads 0-50 in 0.002-in steps; one revolution = 0.050 in of cut depth (CW lowers).
Dovetail slide + gib, backlash removed by a spring-loaded Teflon plug (never remove).
Hard stop presets finish depth for identical strips; nylon side pads (moly-impregnated) let it slide, set to 0.628-0.629 in apart with the supplied jig.
Carbide inserts install with tops parallel to the pocket (pocket angle matches the head); rotate/pair inserts to double edge life.

chapters.title: Hold Down Shoe
chapters.purpose: Spring-loaded shoe that centers the strip under the cutters.
key_facts: Stainless; mounts in the cutter head's center hole; rides ahead of the cutters so it doesn't affect accuracy.
Use once the strip has an apex; critical for slender tips and stiff quad strips.
Slotted shoe angles 61.5 / 73.5 / 91.5 deg for 6/5/4-strip; arrow indicates travel direction; clean with alcohol / dry graphite only (never oil).

chapters.title: Adjustable Bed & Base
chapters.purpose: Base mill-stop/letter system and the push/pull taper screws.
key_facts: Mill stop mounts in one of the base's tapped holes and is moved fore/aft while milling; the holes correspond to the anvil's hold-down stations, giving an automatic stop per station.
Letters A-K stamped on the base side and matched on the bed below the finishing anvils' hold-down screws locate the mill stop.
Set taper: loosen the cap-head (pull) screw, turn the hex-head (push) set screw in/out to change the bar gap; don't over-tighten (warps the bed).
key_numbers: Bed 5/8 x 3/4 x 68 in; screws on 5-in centers; bed attaches to base with 14 cap-head (pull) screws

chapters.title: Bamboo Strip Preparation
chapters.purpose: Culm selection, splitting/node-matching, straightening, heat-treating for milling.
key_facts: Reject deep cuts, big dark splotches, and node heat marks; power fibers must run the full glued-section depth.
Always mill butt->tip; mark the butt end. Common three/three node match; avoid nodes at cut ends, ferrules, tiptop.
Straighten with heat (gun 350-450 F), remove twist (esp. first 18 in of butts); square or slightly inward-taper strip sides.
Heat-treat to light brown (raises MOE, resists set); black = brittle. Remove max material before treating (harder after); rest treated strips >=1 week to regain moisture.
key_numbers: Buy >=10 (ideally 20+) poles
Butt wall 5/16-1/2 in, tip 3/16-5/16 in
Node spacing butt 9-14 in, tip 14-20 in
Rough sections >=6 in over finish (+~2 in butt for the anvil screw); split ~1/8 in wide

chapters.title: Measuring Block
chapters.purpose: Caliper-mounted block to read strip height per geometry.
key_facts: Grooves 61+/73+/91+ for 6/5/4-strip; calibrate with a #38 (0.100 in) drill blank.
Groove constants (drill height): 61+ 0.152, 73+ 0.140, 91+ 0.123 in; add 0.100/0.200 in when a strip exceeds 0.100 in.
Glue up ~6 measured sections to verify, since glue/pressure shift results slightly; record your own constants.

chapters.title: Milling Strips
chapters.purpose: Actually cutting the strips: technique, rough vs finish anvils, and matching the mill-stop letter to the section.
key_facts: Always cut butt->tip; grip behind the adjusting head (never on it) with centered downward pressure; take many light passes and re-cut the first 2-3 in of each pass to full depth.

Rough on a wide roughing anvil (strip + mill stop in hole A) to a 61.5-deg bevel just wider than the anvil; mount the hold-down shoe once an apex forms; then switch to a finishing anvil and set the taper.
Measure strip HEIGHT three ways: micrometer + height/width chart, thread-wrapped strips, or the aluminum measuring block (most accurate); don't measure the apex directly (leftover 'fuzz').
Finish in two stages: cut ~0.015 in oversize, then install fresh sharp cutters and finish at 0.001-0.002 in/pass; remove apex fuzz before gluing and saw off the thick held-down butt.
MILL-STOP LETTER: the strip tip anchors between stations #12-#13; the stop letter usually equals the bamboo hold-down letter; a 7 ft rod uses hole D (ferrule/tiptop at #12).
key_numbers: Min strip width tip 0.200 in / butt 0.250 in
Tip hold-down 2-56 (#43 drill), butt 4-40 (1/8 in), hole ~1 in from butt
Rough passes ~0.010 in; finish 0.001-0.002 in; dial ~0.002 in per hash mark
7 ft #4wt example (#12 ferrule): strip height 0.096 in at ferrule (station #12), 0.033 in at tiptop

chapters.title: Hollow Fluting Cutter
chapters.purpose: Attachment that hollows the strip centers to cut weight (Stoner/Winston flower cross-section).
key_facts: Rollers in 64/76/94 deg (64 std for 6-strip); leave the rod SOLID under ferrules with a ~2.5 in transition; hollow after finish-cutting, butt->tip.
Suggested wall 0.070 in (trout) / 0.085 in (steelhead-salmon); hollowing loses stiffness so increase section area ~2-5% to compensate.
Never adjust the bed by more than 0.020 in between 5-in stations or you may permanently damage it (matters for 3-piece / spey shim setups).
key_numbers: 6 inserts, 11-deg rake, tip radii 1/32, 3/64, 1/16 in
Transition over 2.5 in (anvil fastener spacing); shims ~0.030 in typical

chapters.title: Swelled Butt Kit
chapters.purpose: Shim kit + procedure to raise the finishing anvil for a swelled butt.
key_facts: Max swell 0.060 in per strip / 0.120 in finished rod (do not exceed -- anvil damage); initial rise over 2.5 in.
100 shims in 0.060/0.030/0.020/0.010 in; combine to reach finished swells of 0.020-0.120 in in 0.020 steps.
Leave the swell space unshimmed so the anvil rises there; set the bed tight to the base two stations past the swell; mill the swell with light 0.001-0.002 in cuts.
key_numbers: Anvil hold-down 8-32 flat-head every 2.5 in
Example: 0.100 in finished swell = 0.050 in/strip via 0.030 + 0.020 in shim per space

chapters.title: Magic Star Cutter
chapters.purpose: Alternate hollowing attachment cutting an inverted-T with central support spokes.
key_facts: Square vs triangle inserts; square removes more but leaves ~80% of the triangle's glue seam (weaker); spoke width adjustable 0.030-0.065 in.
As with fluting: solid under ferrules, hollow after finish-cutting butt->tip, and increase rod diameter to offset lost stiffness.
Uses a longer hold-down shoe (inserts sit lower); remove only the top fuzz or you void the star center.
key_numbers: Suggested wall 0.060-0.070 in (trout) / 0.075-0.085 in (steelhead-salmon)
Inserts 1/4 in IC, 1/32 in radius, 11-deg rake; C-2 carbide

chapters.title: Extension Bed
chapters.purpose: 36 in bolt-on bed for one-piece rods up to ~7 ft 6 in.
key_facts: A one-piece strip is cut on BOTH finishing anvils, switching the strip once; rough the tip then butt, finish the butt then tip.
You must know the full taper at 5-in intervals; the tip-butt transition lands between stations #7-#8 (mark it on the bed).
When finishing the butt on the tip anvil, drop the tip-portion stations (station #8 by 0.015 in, #9-#10 another 0.015 in, #11-#13 level with #10) so the butt cut doesn't dig into the tip.
Plane stop: hole B for rough and finish butt, hole A for finish tip.
key_numbers: One-piece capacity ~7 ft 6 in; extension bed 36 in
Strip length = rod + 4 in tip + 5 in butt + 2 in hold-down (e.g., 7 ft -> 95 in)
Tiptop at station #12 with 4 in of strip past it

chapters.title: Enamel Scraper / Strip Flattener
chapters.purpose: 60-deg-groove anvils (with the dial holder/shaver) to scrape enamel off beveled strips.
key_facts: Two anvils with a ~0.250 in-deep 60-deg groove, no taper, held +/-0.0015 in; require the dial-indicator holder/shaving tool.
Bed must have NO taper when shaving; cut the groove so beveled strips protrude enough to shave the enamel; a strong spring means extra downward plane pressure.
The 60-deg groove seats 5-/4-strip splines adequately though not perfectly.

chapters.title: Reference Information
chapters.purpose: Recommended books/sites, the owners' list server, and insert specs.
key_facts: No book covers the Hand Mill itself; recommends Garrison & Carmichael 'A Master's Guide...' (the amateur 'bible'), Howell 'The Lovely Reed', Maurer & Elser, Ray Gould, and Stoner/McLane encyclopedias.
Tom Morgan runs a private owners' list server (join by email); cites RodDNA.com and hexrod.net as free taper sources with Hand Mill station settings (incl. quads and pentas).
Regular inserts: TPGW-321, 3/8 in inscribed circle, 0.015 in tip radius; since July 2011 supplied inserts are C5 carbide (harder), 15% relief, TiN-coated relief edge, diamond-lapped top.

chapters.title: Anvils
chapters.purpose: The plastic anvils that support strips, their variants, hold-down stations, and truing. Full mechanics in machine.anvils.
key_facts: 5 anvils (butt/tip roughing, butt/tip finishing x2); anvils only SUPPORT the strip -- the bed sets the taper.
Finishing anvils have 11 lettered (A-K) hold-down stations; roughing anvils have 3 (long/medium/short).
Finishing anvils must be trued flat (+/-0.001 in) with the dial-holder/shaver before use; never recut the factory reference anvil.

chapters.title: Setting a Taper
chapters.purpose: How the bed is raised every 5 in to set a taper vs. measuring strip height while milling. Full model in setting_model.
key_facts: Bed stations #0-#13 at 5-in centers (0-60 in); #0 fixed to base; taper referenced from ~station #2 (=0.000).
The 'setting' at each station is the cumulative bed rise = caneDNA's total_increase; strip height is measured during milling, not set by the bed.
Morgan says of RodDNA's MHM report: use Station #, Increment, Rod Dim, Increase; DISREGARD Form Depth and Settings.
